name: synchrony
desc: Simple deobfuscator for mangled or obfuscated JavaScript files
why: A JavaScript deobfuscator is a legitimate way to take code apart, though fairly conventional.

brief.what_it_is: Synchrony is a command-line tool and web page that takes a mangled or obfuscated JavaScript file and writes out a cleaned-up version. The README says it is aimed mainly at output from javascript-obfuscator and obfuscator.io. The web version at deobfuscate.relative.im has a Deobfuscate button and a Save button, with results shown in an output panel. The CLI reads a .js file and writes a .cleaned.js file next to it.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no separate motivation. It describes the project as a javascript cleaner and deobfuscator, primarily for javascript-obfuscator and obfuscator.io output.
brief.how_it_works: The README says there is no user configuration yet and that the string decoder runs automatically. It mentions AST visitors, and its error output reads 'Caught an error while attempting to run AST visitor!', which suggests the code is transformed as a syntax tree. The README does not describe the transforms in more detail.

commands_seen.context: Installs the CLI globally from npm. The README's alternatives are yarn global add deobfuscator and pnpm install --global deobfuscator.
Installs from the Git master branch instead of npm. Yarn and pnpm equivalents are given in the README.
Downloads a sample obfuscated file from a gist to use as a test input.
Runs the deobfuscator on the sample file. This is the main CLI invocation.
Prints the cleaned output. The README's step text says the result is at script.cleaned.js, but the command reads obfuscated.cleaned.js, which matches the input filename.

brief.install_notes: The README covers installing from npm (npm, yarn, or pnpm, with --global) or from the Git master branch. The npm package is named deobfuscator while the executable is synchrony. No accounts, API keys, or runtime setup are mentioned beyond Node-style package managers. There is no user configuration to set up.
brief.standout: It is narrowly scoped to javascript-obfuscator and obfuscator.io output and does not ask for any configuration; the string decoder runs on its own. The README is also blunt that artifacts from old javascript-obfuscator versions will likely not deobfuscate and that users should not file issues for them.
brief.status: Unknown. The homepage shows version 2.2.0. I did not see a release date, last commit date, or any note about maintenance status in the README or homepage.
brief.caveats: Old javascript-obfuscator artifacts will likely not deobfuscate correctly, and the README asks users not to open issues for them; try an older synchrony or another tool. There is no configuration. Transformer errors need the full terminal output and the obfuscated file attached to an issue, not screenshots or partial output. The npm package name (deobfuscator) differs from the command name (synchrony). I did not check the license.
quotes: A simple deobfuscator for mangled or obfuscated JavaScript files
There is no user configuration as of yet, the string decoder works automatically
Artifacts produced by old versions of javascript-obfuscator will likely not deobfuscate correctly, please DO NOT open an issue.
